transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-17 16:00 PT - Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Devon Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Kapoor (Redwood Partner PM); Rafael Gomez (Aurora PM), Priya Shah (Aurora Solutions), Liam O'Neal (Aurora Marketplace Ops)

[00:00] Alicia Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the technical steps for the marketplace listing and the ref arch for the joint solution, um quick round robin?
[00:10] Rafael Gomez: yep thanks Alicia, Rafael here, we're primarily focused on getting a private listing that can deploy into our customers' VPCs and also a standard marketplace listing for quick onboarding
[00:20] Priya Shah: and we want to make sure the private deployment supports our VPC peering and KMS patterns, also compliance folks will want to see audit logs
[00:30] Devon Chen: perfect, from Redwood side we have two paths: hosted listing (Redwood hosted or marketplace SaaS) and private/VPC packaged deploy (AMI/container plus orchestration templates). For private we typically provide a reference architecture, terraform modules, and a runbook for KMS and SSO.
[00:48] Liam O'Neal: are you able to support SAML SSO and SSO provisioning for our marketplace customers? sometimes the marketplace requires SSO via their IdP bridge
[00:55] Maya Kapoor: yes we support SAML and OIDC, we have a standard SAML metadata bundle and also a SCIM/SSO integration pattern, small caveat sometimes the naming of attributes changes across IdPs so we recommend a short mapping doc
[01:10] Rafael Gomez: ok good. On the listing side Aurora needs an AMI or container image plus a validated deployment guide and an SLA statement, and we also have a security review which asks for SOC2 docs and network diagrams
[01:23] Alicia Park: noted. we can share our SOC2 summary and the redwood private deployment guide. question: for customers that want dedicated capacity, is that part of the marketplace listing or a separate procurement?
[01:35] Priya Shah: typically separate but we link to it from the listing, we want to be clear about pricing and the onboarding flow
[01:42] Devon Chen: for dedicated: we provide a dedicated deployment profile, and our runtime can be installed either managed by Redwood in customer VPC or packaged for customer-managed infra. We should map the two variants in the reference arch doc
[01:55] Speaker 1: so on the networking side, can you walk through port requirements and peering steps?
[02:01] Devon Chen: yeah quick overview: control-plane (api) endpoints to Redwood-managed control plane, plus worker traffic stays within customer VPC when using private deploy. Ports: outbound 443 for control plane, and internal gRPC over TCP 1967 (example) between controllers and workers; also optional SSH for debug if customer opts in. We'll include an explicit port table in the doc.
[02:25] Priya Shah: encryption at rest — we need KMS integration pattern, the marketplace security questionnaire expects key rotation details
[02:31] Alicia Park: we use customer-managed KMS for private deployment, we can provide key policy examples and note that for hosted we handle keys but for private we provide KMS integration guide
[02:42] Rafael Gomez: great. Another ask: Aurora requires audit logs to be exported to their logging endpoint or to an S3 bucket with lifecycle rules — is that supported?
[02:52] Devon Chen: yes we have audit log exporters; we can push to S3 or to a syslog endpoint, we'll document supported sinks.
[03:02] Alicia Park: on the marketplace listing metadata, we should confirm packaging: container image hosted on ECR or GCR, or AMI for AWS marketplace. Aurora, which do you prefer for the initial listing?
[03:12] Liam O'Neal: AMI is preferred for AWS marketplace but container is acceptable for our cloud marketplace flow. Let's aim for AMI + container artifacts if possible
[03:20] Devon Chen: ok we can produce both, we'll need build artifact access; we'll provide an image manifest and AMI build instructions in the repo.
[03:29] Priya Shah: about the security review, can you send SOC2 attestation and penetration test summary? their security team wants the latest reports
[03:36] Alicia Park: yes, we'll share SOC2 summary and an internal pentest overview (redacted) and a contact for our security review.
[03:43] Rafael Gomez: any compliance/regulatory constraints for data residency? some of our customers need EU-only infra
[03:49] Devon Chen: we support region pinning, and for private deploy we'd recommend deploying workers in the customer's regional VPC; for hosted we can route to EU region cluster. We'll note data locality options in the ref arch.
[03:59] Speaker 2: timeline question — how long to produce the reference arch and docs?
[04:03] Alicia Park: we can have a first draft of the reference architecture, including diagrams and checklist, by 2026-05-21. Runbooks and AMI/container manifests by 2026-05-24.
[04:15] Priya Shah: sounds good. then a staging test the week of 5/25?
[04:19] Rafael Gomez: yes we'll allocate time for a test listing and verify SSO and KMS flows
[04:25] Devon Chen: couple of technical notes — our runtime supports prefix/KV cache and batching; if Aurora customers want deterministic latency we recommend the dedicated profile and quantization settings. For marketplace customers that pick hosted, we'll bias routing to hosted model variants for lower operational overhead
[04:45] Priya Shah: will need a short doc on performance profile and recommended instance types for reference arch — helps buyers estimate cost
[04:51] Devon Chen: we'll include a cost/instance table and expected token throughput per instance class (e.g., 8x A100 equivalence, numbers illustrative).
[04:59] Liam O'Neal: marketing/asset ask — can Redwood provide a short product blurb and 2-3 screenshots for the marketplace listing?
[05:06] Alicia Park: yes marketing assets and a short blurb, and a one-pager for joint solution. We'll send those to Maya who will coordinate co-branded materials.
[05:14] Maya Kapoor: I'll collate assets and send a draft copy to Rafael and Alicia by 2026-05-20
[05:20] Speaker 3: any blockers expected?
[05:23] Rafael Gomez: main blockers are security review timeline and AMI publishing approvals. If we get the SOC2 and runbook quickly we can expedite
[05:31] Alicia Park: ok recap of next steps: Redwood sends ref arch + SOC2 summary by 5/21, Devon sends runbook + AMI manifests by 5/24, Aurora shares listing requirements and staging access by 5/20, schedule staging test week of 5/25 and follow-up call 5/28.
[05:48] Priya Shah: thanks everyone, this was helpful
[05:51] Alicia Park: thanks all, we'll follow-up in email with links

End of transcript
